subject: ela
intro: Fifth graders analyze multiple accounts of the same event or topic, noting important similarities and differences in the point of view the accounts represent. Different writers may emphasize different facts or show different opinions, so comparing accounts gives a fuller, more balanced understanding.

items.prompt:
Two newspaper articles describe the same game. One focuses on the winning team's great plays; the other focuses on the losing team's mistakes.

How do their points of view DIFFER?

steps: Each article emphasizes a different side.
One praises the winners; the other blames the losers.
So they differ in which side they focus on.
solution.answer: One focuses on the winners' success; the other on the losers' mistakes.

items.prompt:
Both accounts of a flood agree that the river overflowed.

What do they have in COMMON?

steps: So they agree on that basic fact.

items.prompt: Why is it useful to read MORE than one account of an event?

steps: Each account may leave out or emphasize different facts.
Reading several gives a fuller, more balanced picture.
solution.answer: To get a fuller, more balanced understanding.

items.prompt: Two accounts that stress different facts differ in ____.
Facts both accounts agree on are their ____.
Reading several accounts gives a more ____ view.
